sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier is closest to I. platycephalus: the two are similar in size and both have a dorsoventrally flattened head capsule; but in this species antennal segment 3 is shorter and the mandibular teeth are more prominent, and the eye spot of the major soldier is projecting in this species, whereas it is not projecting in the major soldier of I. platycephalus. Among the dark-coloured group the alate is closest to I. platycephalus, but the pigmentation of this species is slightly paler; I. platycephalus lacks pale spots at the setal insertions on the vertex, and the two are similar in size.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Major soldier: in dorsal view the vertex and labrum are rusty orange; the frons is dark chestnut brown anteriorly and chestnut brown posteriorly; antennal segment 3 is the darkest, deep brown (sepia brown), segments 1 and 2 paler and pale brown, the remaining segments pale brown; the mandible base is pale chestnut brown, the rest black; the frontal sutures are very pale; the eye spot is white; the head capsule is rusty orange; the postmentum is darker anteriorly, slightly darker than the orange-yellow genae. Thoracic tergites, abdominal tergites and sternites and the legs are pale yellowish white; tibiae and tarsi pale brown, the tibial spurs and claws distinctly coloured; the pronotum has a pale orange tinge. In dorsal view the head capsule is narrow and elongate, its sides nearly parallel; the eye spot projects slightly; the posterior corners are evenly rounded, the posterior margin almost straight. Mandibles robust, with a shallow hump at the base; the apical hook is distinct. The frontal surface is very finely granulate, including the frontal and antennal ridges; the frontal carina is moderately distinct. Labrum medium-sized, ligulate, with long setae at the apex. Antennae 10—12 segmented, usually 11, the relative length formula 2<3>4=5; antennal segment 3 is stoutly clavate and as long as segments 4 and 5 together. Vertex with about 6 moderately long setae; frons with about 10 short or very short setae. Anterior margin of the pronotum distinct, incised at about 150°, the sides slightly convergent, the posterior margin slightly concave. In lateral and oblique view the head capsule is strongly dorsoventrally flattened and planar; the frons slopes very gently at 30° from the vertex; the eye spot is large and oval; the mandibles are moderately upcurved; the hind femur is strongly inflated. Minor soldier: colour similar to the major soldier but slightly paler, the frons rusty anteriorly and rusty orange posteriorly and on the vertex; the mandible base pale chestnut brown, the apex very dark chestnut brown; the frontal granulation finer than in the major soldier; the frontal sutures absent; the eye spot not projecting; the mandibles slightly less robust than in the major soldier; the head capsule about 2/3 the length of that of the major soldier but proportionally wider, its sides distinctly divergent (nearly parallel in the major soldier); pigmentation and sclerotization of the frons and antennal ridges weaker than in the major soldier; the hind femur moderately inflated; other characters as in the major soldier. Measurements — major soldier (n=5, range/mean±standard deviation): head length including mandibles 2.73—3.12/2.89±0.18 mm, head length to the postclypeus 1.94—2.37/2.13±0.19 mm, maximum head width 1.11—1.18/1.14±0.027 mm, width across the antennal ridges 1.05—1.13/1.08±0.031 mm, head height (excluding postmentum) 0.72—0.83/0.77±0.054 mm, maximum labrum width 0.31—0.36/0.34±0.025 mm, left mandible length 0.98—1.10/1.04±0.043 mm, postmentum length 1.46—1.68/1.59±0.12 mm, maximum width 0.46—0.49/0.47±0.012 mm and minimum width 0.16—0.23/0.20±0.026 mm, maximum pronotum width 1.13—1.26/1.19±0.066 mm, maximum length 0.95—1.10/1.02±0.060 mm, hind femur length 0.74—0.83/0.79±0.039 mm and width 0.51—0.60/0.56±0.039 mm, hind tibia length 0.85—0.93/0.90±0.035 mm, body length 7.10—7.81/7.47±0.33 mm. Minor soldier (n=9, range/mean±standard deviation (holotype)): head length including mandibles 2.17—2.37/2.28±0.059 (2.25) mm, head length to the postclypeus 1.46—1.70/1.58±0.072 (1.58) mm, maximum head width 1.03—1.23/1.00±0.034 (1.01) mm (as in the original), width across the antennal ridges 0.88—1.00/0.94±0.038 (0.96) mm, head height (excluding postmentum) 0.65—0.72/0.69±0.024 (0.69) mm, maximum labrum width 0.29—0.31/0.30±0.008 (0.29) mm, left mandible length 0.92—1.00/0.97±0.032 (1.00) mm, postmentum length 1.00—1.08/1.04±0.027 (1.05) mm, maximum width 0.38—0.43/0.41±0.018 (0.43) mm and minimum width 0.16—0.23/0.19±0.021 (0.21) mm, maximum pronotum width 0.90—1.05/0.99±0.049 (1.01) mm, maximum length 0.62—0.80/0.71±0.061 (0.72) mm, hind femur length 0.60—0.75/0.65±0.045 (0.65) mm and width 0.29—0.39/0.33±0.029 (0.33) mm, hind tibia length 0.69—0.74/0.71±0.018 (0.70) mm, body length 5.40—6.25/5.79±0.29 (5.40) mm.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: In dorsal view uniformly dark brown (sepia brown), including the sclerotized veins of the fore wing; wing membrane pale brown, without iridescent lustre. Frons and vertex dark brown, pale only in the minute spots at the setal insertions. Pronotum and abdominal tergites dark brown. Thoracic tergites with a distinct median line. Antennae, labrum and legs pale brown. Sternites pale brown. Tibiae slightly paler than the femora. Head short-oval; coronal suture absent. Compound eyes very small for the genus, moderately projecting, slightly elongate, almost straight along the antennal socket. Ocelli small, oval, touching the compound eye. Antennae 13—16 segmented, mostly 14—15, usually with the formula 2<3>4=5, variable because the elongation of segment 3 is slight. Lateral margins of the pronotum with moderate to long setae; the anterior margin evenly and shallowly concave, the posterior margin slightly concave, the sides slightly convex; the transverse band and median line distinct. The radius reaches the anterior margin of the fore wing at about 1/3 of the wing length from the suture; the radial sector has 5—7 branches. Arolia small. Measurements (n=9, 6 males 3 females, range/mean±standard deviation): head length including labrum 1.01—1.12/1.09±0.055 mm, head length to the postclypeus 0.77—0.90/0.84±0.044 mm, maximum head width (at the compound eyes) 0.83—0.93/0.88±0.034 mm, compound eye diameter (including sclerites) 0.22—0.26/0.25±0.016 mm, minimum distance from the compound eye to the head base 0.11—0.13/0.12±0.006 mm, ocellus diameter 0.08—0.11/0.09±0.007 mm, maximum pronotum width 0.75—0.90/0.83±0.043 mm, maximum length 0.57—0.69/0.63±0.033 mm, body length with wings 7.10—8.52/7.90±0.48 mm, body length without wings 4.69—5.82/5.33±0.49 mm, fore wing length (from the suture) 4.83—5.54/5.29±0.21 mm, maximum fore wing width 1.32—1.38/1.36±0.026 mm.

note: Adapted from the new-species description in Scheffrahn, Austin & Szalanski (2024), original in English; the holotype is a minor soldier; figure numbers (Figs 1—3), localities and collection records are not translated.
